A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FSLoRA research. All 31 pages of v3 and 33 pages of v4, including figures, tables, equations and appendices, support comparison.

before.justification: Table 5.1 and the appendices report original fine-tuning experiments, ablations, heterogeneity tests and gradient measurements.

after.justification: V4 retains original experiments and adds Qwen, FFA-LoRA and stable-rank results in Tables 11, 14 and 15.

M1.justification: The core Random-k updates and aggregation remain unchanged. Appendix J.5 adds an optional importance-weighted sampling variant with inverse-probability rescaling; v3 only tested heuristic importance sampling and described it as biased. Partial participation already existed in v3.

E1.justification: Both versions use GLUE, the eight-task commonsense benchmark, and Wizard, Dolly-15k and Alpaca with MMLU evaluation. Qwen adds a backbone configuration, not new dataset or task coverage. Homogeneous ranks, heterogeneous resources and partial participation were already evaluated.

E2.justification: V4 substantially expands the comparisons: Tables 1–2 add RAVAN and untuned base models to the retained HeteroLoRA, FlexLoRA and FLoRA comparisons. Appendix G.4 newly evaluates FFA-LoRA alongside FedLoRA and FSLoRA under matched local parameter budgets.

E3.justification: New settings include Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct, the equal-trainable-parameter FFA-LoRA comparison, and stable-rank measurements at layer 15 with global rank 32. Table 14 uses local/global ranks 8/8 for FFA-LoRA, 4/4 for FedLoRA and 4/8 for FSLoRA. Existing split and training-budget specifications are retained.

E4.justification: Appendix H adds stable-rank trajectories examining whether global adapters retain richer adaptation structure. Appendix G.4 adds a controlled freezing-versus-sketching comparison. Earlier rank, local-update, dynamic-ratio, heterogeneity and compression analyses remain.

E5.justification: Both versions report three independent runs and ± values in the main accuracy tables. Additional rows follow the existing practice; no new seed disclosures, confidence intervals or significance-testing procedures appear.

E6.justification: The original main FSLoRA averages remain 83.3% and 79.4%. V4 adds RAVAN/base-model scores, Qwen results (FSLoRA average 76.06%), the FFA-LoRA comparison (77.64% versus 69.92%) and stable-rank trajectories. Table C.1 to Table 6 revises spectral-norm/magnitude-sum averages from 73.2/74.2 to 75.4/73.6, reversing their ordering. These are added or revised results, not demonstrated improvements between versions under identical settings.

T1.justification: Assumption 4.1 changes from global smoothness to smoothness on a bounded region containing the iterates. New Appendix J.5 introduces importance-weighted sketches, Lemma J.6, Proposition J.7 and Theorem J.8. Appendix J.4 also corrects an expected-norm equality to an inequality. The original main convergence bound is retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the central contributions: resource-adaptive sketching of global LoRA modules, convergence characterization and improved accuracy/efficiency. Revised emphasis on arbitrary sketching ratios and the FedAvg limit restates claims already present in v3.

C2.justification: V4 explicitly limits its analysis to full participation and identifies asynchronous participation, unstable connections, stragglers and latency fluctuations as uncovered. It adds interpretations of factor freezing, uniform component exposure and stable-rank behavior. The assertion of no additional operations becomes a qualified description of lightweight sketching and padding overhead.

D1.justification: V4 adds an equivalent dense-submatrix implementation explanation and partial-participation pseudocode, and identifies the LLaMA checkpoint as Instruct without establishing a rerun. Existing hyperparameters and the repository link remain. The disclosure of four NVIDIA A100 GPUs with 40 GB each is removed.

R1.justification: V4 adds positioning around RAVAN, Uni-LoRA, additional federated-LLM work and partial-participation theory. It removes the dedicated FedBCGD comparison and its reference. The main positioning against heterogeneous LoRA methods remains; citation-style and bibliographic updates do not constitute new research coverage.

P1.justification: V4 edits the abstract, contributions, algorithm description and analytical discussion, adds descriptive labels to algorithm stages, reorganizes appendices, and introduces Limitations, Impact Statement and Acknowledgments sections. Most existing exposition and the main section sequence remain.

P2.justification: The main paper and references change from single-column formatting to a two-column conference layout. Table 5.1 becomes Tables 1–2; new comparison and diagnostic tables and Algorithm 2 appear, while the FedBCGD table disappears. Figures 5–6 are widened without changing plotted results, and appendix tables and equations are extensively reflowed.

improvement.justification: The budget-matched FFA-LoRA comparison, additional diagnostics and dense-submatrix explanation strengthen empirical support and clarity. However, new Eq. (60) treats pi_i = k*w_i/sum(w) as a without-replacement inclusion probability: r=3, k=2 and weights (3,1,1) give pi_1=1.2. This undermines the added unbiasedness claim and the argument supporting Theorem J.8. These empirical and explanatory benefits coexist with a substantive new theoretical defect, preventing a reliable net quality judgment.
